entries.04191b4966966fa3: This business provides, in Japan, leasing and loans and investment (finance), together with related services, for information and communications equipment, office equipment, industrial machine tools, transportation equipment, and commercial and service industry facilities, among others. Sales to external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥462,066 million (up 2.9% year on year), the largest of the 5 reportable segments. Net income attributable to owners of the parent was ¥22,810 million, almost the same level as ¥22,836 million in the previous year. NTT TC Lease Co., Ltd. (general leasing, an equity-method affiliate), a joint venture with the NTT Group, is cited as an initiative in this business field.

entries.2a8f9df5117f60cd: This is the car rental business operated by Nippon Rent-A-Car Service, Inc., a consolidated subsidiary (car rental business, voting rights ownership 88.6%). In the fiscal year ended March 2026, it captured high utilization rates and strong inbound demand, and set a new record high for profit. It has also signed an agreement to acquire all shares of Bargain Car Rentals Australia Pty Ltd, an independent Australian car rental company, which would be its first investment in an overseas car rental business made on its own.
entries.2c660412b10962b0: It is advancing grid-scale storage batteries, which absorb output fluctuations from renewable energy and stabilize the power grid, as a pillar of its growth strategy.
entries.2fef2bc835001015: This business covers auto leasing for corporate and individual customers, car rental, car sharing, and other services. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥314,948 million (up 4.7% year on year). Profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥12,131 million, down from ¥17,685 million in the previous fiscal year. While car rental grew on high utilization rates and inbound demand, corporate auto leasing was hurt by higher funding costs, an increase in selling, general and administrative expenses, and the recording of impairment losses related to systems.

entries.32aae7d43aa0ade4: This is CSI Leasing, Inc., a consolidated subsidiary (U.S., general leasing business, voting rights ownership 100.0%). In the fiscal year ended March 2026, it performed well, mainly in Central and South America, and also recorded gains on the sale of a U.S. data center and operating investment securities. It has acquired a majority stake in Aeroservicios USA, Inc., a specialist in aircraft ground support equipment (GSE), and has established a structure to handle equipment from introduction through disposal. The company's revenue (including its consolidated subsidiaries, excluding intercompany internal sales within the consolidated group) was ¥172,811 million, exceeding 10% of consolidated revenue.

entries.57fb40458e124c73: The business is divided into five [[term:segment|segments]]. entries.76eaf28762da8316: Tokyo Century Corporation is a financial services company centered on leasing and finance. Its predecessor was Century Leasing System Co., Ltd., established in July 1969 through joint investment by four companies including Itochu Corporation; it merged with Tokyo Leasing Co., Ltd. in April 2009 and changed its trade name to Tokyo Century Corporation in October 2016. It is listed on the Prime Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange, and its accounting standards are Japanese GAAP. Itochu Corporation is listed as another affiliated company.
entries.772e442d43acae0a: Consolidated revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,457,670 million, up 6.5% from ¥1,368,635 million in the previous fiscal year. Revenue from external customers was largest in the Domestic Leasing Business at ¥462,066 million, followed by Specialty Business at ¥342,981 million, Automobility Business at ¥314,948 million, International Business at ¥270,900 million, and Environmental Infrastructure Business at ¥66,081 million. International Business revenue increased 21.7% from ¥222,652 million in the previous fiscal year. Profit movements by business are explained as lease revenue, gains on vehicle sales, ship sales revenue and power generation businesses.

entries.836299ffc9c84d60: It is advancing grid-scale storage batteries, which absorb output fluctuations from renewable energy and stabilize the power grid, as a pillar of its growth strategy. It aims to start operations at a scale of about 600 MW.

entries.ef18b884ffc394a2: [[term:net-income-attributable-to-owners-of-parent|Net income attributable to owners of parent]] for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥111,299 million, up 30.5% from ¥85,279 million in the previous fiscal year. Profit of reportable segments is on the basis of this net income: Specialty Business ¥112,179 million (increase due to insurance settlements related to Russia in the aircraft business, among others), International Business ¥23,540 million, Domestic Leasing Business ¥22,810 million, and Automobility Business ¥12,131 million. Environmental Infrastructure Business recorded a loss of ¥44,450 million, mainly due to impairment losses related to the biomass co-firing power generation business. Funds for leasing and lending are raised through borrowings from domestic and overseas financial institutions and through bonds, commercial paper and others, and the increase in funding costs is explained as a burden on the Domestic Leasing Business and the Automobility Business.

entries.f36b7dba96503f78: This business engages in domestic and overseas power generation related to renewable energy and other sources, as well as leasing and finance. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥66,081 million (up 8.6% year on year). Profit attributable to owners of the parent was a loss of ¥44,450 million, turning into a deficit from ¥818 million in profit in the previous fiscal year. Earnings excluding gains on the sale of the solar power business and one-off factors were solid, but the recording of impairment losses related to the biomass co-firing power business outweighed them.
entries.f66e88cc135aa5f5: This business provides leasing, loans and equity investment (finance), and related services in Japan and overseas, covering specialized assets such as ships, aircraft and real estate. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥342,981 million (up 2.5% year on year). Profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥112,179 million, a large increase from ¥32,872 million in the previous fiscal year. The main factors behind the increase in profit were the recording of Russia-related insurance settlement income in the aircraft business, among other things; in the ship business, there were a decrease in revenue from ship sales and foreign exchange valuation losses.
